Oleg noticed a few races with the TASK_WAKING usage on fork.
- since TASK_WAKING is basically a spinlock
- since we set TASK_WAKING (*) without holding rq->lock it could
be there still is a rq->lock holder
Cure the second issue by not setting TASK_WAKING in sched_fork()
only temporarily in wake_up_new_task() while calling select_task_rq().
Cure the first by holding rq->lock around the select_task_rq() call

column2: this however requires that we push down the

column1: rq->lock release into select_task_rq_fair()'s cgroup stuff.
Because select_task_rq_fair() still needs to drop the rq->lock we
cannot fully get rid of TASK_WAKING.
